Field.u1: Why is the rootworm risk high if it's November?
Field.a1: Because the 2026 plan has corn here again — a third year in a row. Beetles lay eggs in the soil of corn fields, and next year the larvae feed on corn roots. The longer corn follows corn, the more of them build up.
Field.a2: Changing the crop works best. I compared options for this field:
Field.o_b_v: +$50 per acre a year · low rootworm risk
Field.o_c_v: −$75 per acre a year · low rootworm risk

Rec.search: Ask the assistant or find a field
Rec.nf1: The owner asked a question about Pivot 12
Rec.nf3: Pivot 14 check: 17% of plants with aphids
Rec.title: Corn rootworm on Pivot 12
Rec.sub: Risk for the 2026 season · decide by 15 February, when seed is ordered
Rec.do: Change the crop for 2026. It's the most effective measure against rootworm, and it improves the rotation too.
Rec.accept: Accept and add to the owner report
Rec.e1: Corn in 2024 and 2025, and corn again in the 2026 plan.
Rec.e2_t: Larvae hatch from late May into June
Rec.e2: When the soil has built up enough heat, larvae hatch and look for corn roots. Here that's usually late May into June.
Rec.e2_src: Soil degree days · NASA POWER, 18 years · model threshold under review
Rec.e2_label: Soil heat build-up over the season and the larval hatch window
Rec.e3: After a different crop, larvae find no food and die. After corn, they survive and damage the roots.
Rec.o1: For example alfalfa, soybean or sorghum. Compare rotations to see the effect on profit and water.
Rec.o2: Check the roots in June and set beetle traps in July to judge whether action is needed.
Rec.o3: Discuss with your seed supplier. Terrasight doesn't recommend specific products.
Rec.unknown: There are no beetle counts from this field for 2025. If you have them, add them and the estimate gets sharper.
Rec.msg: Hello! Pivot 12 is planned for corn again in 2026 — a third year in a row. That sharply raises the risk of corn rootworm, whose larvae damage the roots. I suggest changing the crop: alfalfa fits best and also earns more. Let's discuss before 15 February, before seed is ordered.
Rec.s3: Soil degree-day model (university extension model, threshold under review)
Rec.tf1: Corn on this field for 3 years in a row
Rec.tf2: Larvae hatch at ~380 °C·days — expected in June
Rec.tf3: Beetles were reported in Finney County last summer

Assistant.q: Which fields will suffer most if the winter is dry?
Assistant.a1: Two fields with no residue are most at risk: North strip and Pivot 21. Wind will blow the dry topsoil away, and they'll have the least water in spring. Wheat on Pivot 3 and South strip has water in reserve and covers the soil — a dry winter barely hurts it.
